intelligence.enrichment: Habitat interactions can occur between biotic and abiotic components, between two abiotic components, or among biotic components. The identities of the interacting components determine the interaction type and the life process or habitat feature affected. The learner correctly applies this rule: Habitat interactions can occur between biotic and abiotic components, between two abiotic components, or among biotic components. Every habitat interaction is mainly a living thing affecting another living thing.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Ecosystems and habitats. The student must decide: Classify an interaction in a habitat as biotic-abiotic, abiotic-abiotic, or biotic-biotic by identifying what kinds of components are interacting. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Retarget the source onto this Science decision. Keep the source item type. Recalculate the key.
